description:
We are Team Lunar Capital.

We are a team of passionate student innovators dedicated to making space exploration accessible, engaging, and meaningful for the next generation. We believe that learning complex engineering principles doesn't require advanced degrees—it starts with curiosity, play, and clear choices.
summary: A team made of two 17-year-old boys that each handled the code and presentation of a game called Moon Outpost. Moon Outpost is a free browser game where kids aged 7 to 12 build a moon base over the span of three days. Players mine rocks, split limited generator power between life support, greenhouse and radiation shield, and survive flares and asteroids. It exists because space education often stays abstract, so kids never get to see real mission trade-offs. Flare warnings use real NASA DONKI data, and every choice costs something: sprinting burns air, and shielding takes power from food. Points come from banked rocks, so risky, far-away, rare ores pay more but can cost your bag. Daily goals unlock each outpost stage, so players must stay alive while chasing points. Space School and quizzes explain the science in plain words.
details:
How was it made?
The project/game was made with the help of AI, Claude, with Vercel as the website host and Anti Gravity to help restructure the code and find its flaws.

What to expect in the game?
The game started with the menu offering options to play, tutorial for the introduction of the game, settings to customise with the gameplay and space schools offering short and simple explanations regarding events that happened in space, e.g., solar flares, asteroid showers, etc. The space schools also give quizzes to test knowledge that obtained from the earlier session. The difficulty is being separated into easier and harder. The main game gives the option to choose the difficulty of the game that is separated into easy, normal and hard. The game also offers different lengths of gameplay, being 5 minutes, 10 minutes and endless. The gameplay itself has the aim to collect the minerals/ores on the moon that were separated into different rarities and higher rarities, equivalent to higher points gained. The point was utilised for upgrades within the game and the determining factor of grade at the end of the game, ranging from D to S. Players also need to survive different space events/weather while managing the resources within the game, such as oxygen, food, and stamina. This game is capable of attracting younger audiences' attention easily and helps them to understand the space even further through the subtle explanation for actions that the player did. We consider various factors such as exposure time and difficulty, offering different lengths of gameplay and harder difficulty for players who are into challenges.
